correctness.rationale: For each unbounded minimal forbidden length n, prefix/suffix witnesses yield a bi-infinite splice with every forbidden A-block covering [0,n), leaving at most ell-n+1 placements. A generator of the product must cover each uniform iid q-symbol partner, giving 1≤sum_{ell≥n}(ell-n+1)|F_ell|q^{-ell}. A growth rate below log q makes this tail vanish, contradiction. Product lifting proves the reverse upper bound. Exact minimal-forbidden and language product identities prove the example triple; finite checker independently tests its language counts and small-length product identities.

value.rationale: Sharp theorem for every non-SFT base and every q≥2: adding an unconstrained q-symbol factor forces at least log q generating obstruction complexity, with an abrupt finite-type boundary. Every zero-h_G non-SFT attains the bound; the explicit 2026 example yields a complete three-entropy product profile (log q,log(2q),log(2q)). The invariant addresses a natural infimum over generating presentations rather than arbitrary fixed finite sizes.
